new_findings.title: Base integration can wait for the review/CI that it must precede
new_findings.scenario: H is valid against B0. Before the next formal review, base advances to B1 and authoritative observation sets integration_required (for example mergeable=false). The G1 version table requires integration and a new H for the triggered branch; G2 for B1 is invalidated and cannot be dispatched before applicable G1. But the integration rule/r12 waits for that same-version review/CI before it creates the only correction batch. If the PR first opens or synchronizes in conflict, the PR-only workflow also cannot run until the conflict is resolved.
new_findings.impact: An ordinary, in-scope base conflict has no stated permitted next step except waiting to timeout/Blocked. The new unconditional integration batching rule conflicts with the retained pre_review_g1 exception; keeping G1-before-G2 and normal bounded correction both requires an explicit ordering rule.
new_findings.smallest_compatible_fix: Use the existing pre_review_g1 correction mechanism with an explicit base_integration reason when an authoritative conflict/human trigger is known before applicable G1/checking can complete. Preserve one writer and one batch, include already known same-version problems, and count once on dispatch. State how any obsolete in-flight work is invalidated/stopped before correction; do not wait for an unstartable review or a conflict-suppressed CI run. When applicable G1 has already passed and review/CI are genuinely in progress, retain normal collection into one batch. After the local merge, require full G1, G2 and G3 on the new real head. Do not mark missing CI successful or introduce a new workflow trigger/platform.
planned_validation_needed: Extend h13/r12 with base conflict before current-version G1/G2 and no CI run: exactly one bounded integration correction, zero premature G2, no missing-CI success, then latest-head G1/G2/G3.
Retain a separate checking-phase case where an existing applicable review is pending: no competing batch and one round when the collected batch dispatches.

new_findings.title: The required merge has no compatible owned scope and Red boundary
new_findings.scenario: A correction finding owns files A and its regression test. The pinned new base also changes unrelated file B. The prescribed git merge must bring B into the worktree and merge commit even if the Implementer only authors an in-scope resolution to A. The assignment only promises a base tip and the batch finding scope; the Red rule requires the entire attempt commit scope to be inside it. The same ambiguity makes g13(a), a clean merge that imports upstream behavior, collide with the general every-behavior-changing-attempt Red rule.
new_findings.impact: The honest merge is either rejected for out-of-scope writes/Red scope, or the implementation must silently exempt arbitrary merge contents. Preserving ancestor commits alone does not make the replacement merge route executable or evidence-valid.
new_findings.smallest_compatible_fix: Bind the integration assignment to its old feature head and exact adopted base tip. Explicitly authorize importing that pinned base and distinguish its unchanged incoming changes from Implementer-authored conflict/fix edits. Keep those authored edits and their regression tests within the approved batch scope; behavior-changing resolutions need genuine original Red bound to a stable integration finding/reason and batch. Define that mechanical adoption of the pinned baseline does not require manufacturing Red for already-existing upstream behavior, while any additional authored change remains checked. If an authored resolution exceeds scope, return through D11. Keep both parents/lineage and new-head Green/review/CI; no general semantic-diff framework is needed.
planned_validation_needed: Extend g13/r12 with an unrelated incoming base path plus an in-scope behavior-changing resolution with its original Red: valid after the declared scope separation.
Add an extra Implementer-authored out-of-scope edit to the same merge: rejected.
Check a clean baseline-only merge does not demand a fabricated original Red, and a behavioral resolution with missing Red still Blocks.
